description: West Virginia-only rules checked against the West Virginia Code and the Division of Motor Vehicles. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Section 17C-6-1 sets a floor, not a single maximum, for controlled-access and interstate highways.

questions.q: Where no special hazard requires a lower speed, the West Virginia limit in a business or residence district is
questions.explanation: Section 17C-6-1(b)(2) sets twenty-five miles per hour in any business or residence district. Those speeds may be altered as authorized in sections 17C-6-2 and 17C-6-3.

questions.q: The speed section 17C-6-1 states for an open-country highway, except as otherwise provided in the chapter, is
questions.explanation: Section 17C-6-1(b)(3) sets fifty-five miles per hour on open country highways, except as otherwise provided by that chapter.

questions.q: On a West Virginia controlled-access or interstate highway, where no special hazard requires a lower speed, section 17C-6-1 says the speed
options: Is 55 mph and the business, school, and open-country limits still apply
Shall be not less than 55 mph, and the limits in subsection (b) do not apply
Is 70 mph whether or not a sign is posted
questions.explanation: Section 17C-6-1(d) says the speed limit on controlled-access highways and interstate highways, where no special hazard exists that requires a lower speed, shall be not less than 55 miles per hour, and the speed limits specified in subsection (b) do not apply. That subsection states a floor. It does not set 55 mph as the interstate maximum.

questions.q: West Virginia's definition of an impaired state includes an alcohol concentration in the blood of
options: Five hundredths of one percent or more
Eight hundredths of one percent or more, by weight
Two hundredths of one percent or more for every driver
Fifteen hundredths of one percent or more only
questions.explanation: Section 17C-5-2(a)(1)(E) defines an impaired state to include a person who has an alcohol concentration in his or her blood of eight hundredths of one percent or more, by weight. The definition also includes being under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, another drug or inhalant, or a combination.

questions.q: A person who drives a commercial motor vehicle in West Virginia with an alcohol concentration in the blood, breath, or urine of four hundredths of one percent or more, by weight, violates
options: Only the general adult impaired-driving section, which uses eight hundredths of one percent
Only the under-21 rule of two hundredths of one percent
questions.explanation: Section 17E-1-14(a) says that, in addition to any other penalties in the code, a person who drives, operates, or is in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle while having an alcohol concentration in the blood, breath, or urine of four hundredths of one percent or more, by weight, violates that section. Subsection (c) separately provides a 24-hour out-of-service order for any measurable alcohol in the system of a person driving a commercial motor vehicle, or for refusing the preliminary breath test described in that subsection.

questions.q: West Virginia sends a warning letter when a driver accumulates at least
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says motorists who accumulate at least six points receive a warning letter. Points for an infraction remain on the record for two years from the conviction date. The violation itself remains for five years.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: A West Virginia driver who accumulates 12 or 13 points is suspended for
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles lists 30 days for 12 to 13 points, 45 days for 14 to 15, 60 days for 16 to 17, 90 days for 18 to 19, and 120 days for 20 or more. Section 17B-3-6(e) also refers to a pending 30-day suspension based on 12 or 13 points.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: An approved West Virginia defensive-driving course may deduct points, if the driver has not reached 14 points, in the amount of
questions.explanation: Section 17B-3-6(e) says the division may, upon completion of an approved defensive-driving course, deduct three points if the licensee has not reached 14 points. A driver notified of a pending 30-day suspension for 12 or 13 points may submit proof of the course and the reinstatement fee before the suspension's effective date to deduct three points and rescind that pending suspension.

questions.q: A West Virginia Level 1 instruction permit is for a driver at least 15 and less than 18. The driver may drive only
options: Between 5 a.m. and 10 p.m., with a driver 21+ in front
At any hour if a parent is somewhere in the vehicle
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says a Level 1 driver must be at least 15 and less than 18, must have a licensed driver 21 or over in the front seat, and may drive only between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. All occupants must use safety belts. The driver may have only two additional non-family passengers besides the supervising adult.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: A West Virginia Level 2 intermediate license requires the driver to be at least 16, to have held a Level 1 permit for six months, and to certify
options: 50 hours, with 10 of those hours at night
No practice hours if a road test is passed
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says Level 2 requires a road-skills test, age of at least 16, a Level 1 permit held for six months, an infraction-free record for the six months immediately before the application, and a 50-hour certification with 10 hours at night, certified by a parent or legal guardian, or a driver-education card.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: During the first six months of West Virginia Level 2, the licensee may not drive with
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says that during the first six months of Level 2 the licensee may not drive with any non-family passenger under 20. During the second six months the licensee may not drive with more than one non-family passenger under 20.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Between 10:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m., a West Virginia Level 2 licensee must be with a supervising adult driver except when driving for
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says a Level 2 driver may drive without a supervising adult between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Between 10:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. a supervising adult must accompany the driver except when the licensee is participating in or returning from employment, a school-sanctioned activity, a religious activity, or an emergency requiring the licensee to drive to prevent bodily injury or death.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Two violations on a West Virginia Level 2 license result in revocation until
options: The driver completes 10 more practice hours
questions.explanation: The Division of Motor Vehicles says that if you receive two violations on a Level 2 license, the license is revoked until your 18th birthday. Level 3 requires the driver to be at least 17 and infraction-free for one year. The page says that one-year count excludes a headlamp violation and an improper backing violation.

provenance.manual: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In West Virginia, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: West Virginia issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: West Virginia car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In West Virginia, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.
questions.remember: West Virginia: hold the permit 6 months.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver's Licensing (GDL) | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in West Virginia complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: West Virginia: 50 hours of supervised driving.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver's Licensing (GDL) | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Of a West Virginia teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: West Virginia: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver's Licensing (GDL) | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In West Virginia, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.
questions.remember: West Virginia: driving alone from 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in West Virginia not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: West Virginia restricts provisional drivers from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: West Virginia new drivers: off the road 10 p.m. to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver's Licensing (GDL) | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In West Virginia, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: West Virginia drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver's Licensing (GDL) | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: How many questions are on the West Virginia car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The West Virginia car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the West Virginia car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 76% to pass the West Virginia car knowledge test.
questions.remember: West Virginia car test: pass with 76%.

questions.q: In West Virginia, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: West Virginia sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In West Virginia, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in West Virginia brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: West Virginia, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in West Virginia?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in West Virginia can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: West Virginia rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes West Virginia's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: West Virginia: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: West Virginia phone law: hands-free only.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in West Virginia?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: West Virginia left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is West Virginia's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: West Virginia seat belt enforcement is primary.
questions.remember: West Virginia seat belts: primary law.

provenance.manual: Occupant Protection | WV Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in West Virginia?
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: West Virginia: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is West Virginia's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: West Virginia requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under West Virginia's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: West Virginia can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.
questions.remember: West Virginia suspension: 12 points in 24 months.

provenance.manual: Point System | WV Division of Motor Vehicles
